body: pushed suggested changes
@Calinou Thanks for the detailed write up. The testing project link didn't work, but I think I managed to fix what you described. Can you recheck?

I'm a little bit confused why `StyleBoxFlat` is receiving texture support when we already have `StyleBoxTexture`. Some of the original ideas in the linked discussions are either related to `StyleBoxTexture` or talk about adding features like gradients or bevels to `StyleBoxFlat`, but not complete texture support. Which would be reasonable.

There are two side-effects from making these changes to the flat stylebox:
- First, it confuses use cases between `StyleBoxFlat` and `StyleBoxTexture`. Why and when pick one over the other? Why are there now cases where you want to use texture but should use `StyleBoxFlat` for it, and not `StyleBoxTexture`? What is the point of having two of them? These are questions that will run through the mind of a user looking at the API.
- Second, it turns `StyleBoxFlat` into a multifunctional beast that can handle most of the situations where a stylebox is needed, rendering functional separation kind of moot. It can be empty, it can be line, it can be flat, and now it can be texture. Granted the first two are just the result of turning things off, but the sum of it is all the same — it's one stylebox that can do too much.

If gradients are desired here, I think what I suggested in the old related PR, #77215, should be the approach. Expose a configurable gradient resource, rather than support for textures. And either use the gradient directly somehow or create a gradient texture implicitly behind the scenes. And if texture-based styleboxes need these customizations, add border texture and shadow texture to `StyleBoxTexture`. Keeps things simpler, more organized, more specialized.

I think there’s also been proposals for adding corner rounding / dropshadows to StyleboxTexture (eg https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/discussions/6846). Maybe we should reconsider if Stylebox seperation into flat/texture is actually something users want.

StyleBoxFlat is already a multi functional beast. It can do almost everything StyleBoxLine can but with rounded corners, shadows, and borders. And with this, it would be able to do almost everything StyleBoxTexture can but with rounded corners, shadows, and borders. 

The code is very complex to add these 3 features to the other StyleBoxes, and would make all of them feel even more redundant IMO. 

I think the value of the other styles would just be explicitness and simplicity

> Maybe we should reconsider if Stylebox seperation into flat/texture is actually something users want.

In my experience, the separation is the result of two different approaches to styling. Flats are used when you start from a simple form, while textures are used when you have a hand-drawn design. I'm not sure that these two have much of an overlap in practice, where textures and simple forms are needed at the same time.

Similar features can just be implemented to both of them as needed, I don't see it as grounds to merging the two together, especially when Godot is not preparing for the next major version where overhaul of the system design is expected.

If a composite look is wanted, though, it would make more sense to add a built-in stylebox type for layering other styleboxes. It can quite easily be made as a custom script, but having one built-in would make it more accessible.

> StyleBoxFlat is already a multi functional beast. It can do almost everything StyleBoxLine can but with rounded corners, shadows, and borders. And with this, it would be able to do almost everything StyleBoxTexture can but with rounded corners, shadows, and borders.

That is exactly what I've said, not really a rebuttal to my points. I just see it as a problem.

I also think explicitness and simplicity should be applied to flats here. There is an explicit request to add gradient support to flats, so let's explicitly add gradient support to flats. Not full texture support with the intent to be used for gradients. If texture styleboxes need rounded corners, then they should be explicitly implemented for texture styleboxes. Handling specific cases for specific needs, rather than making one giant stylebox that does everything.

When one thing does 50 different things, each feature becomes less discoverable, and the whole thing becomes more intimidating. We already have separation. We should leverage it, not muddy its strengths. And if the two styleboxes need to be merged into one, then that's a different discussion. It shouldn't happen as a side-effect of adding some requested feature (but not in the way it has been requested).

So you think instead of exposing a Texture2D, I should specifically expose a GradientTexture2D? Or should I expose specific properties for gradients and reimplement gradient logic in StyleBoxFlat

Both seem a bit excessive just for explicitness

> So you think instead of exposing a Texture2D, I should specifically expose a GradientTexture2D? Or should I expose specific properties for gradients and reimplement gradient logic in StyleBoxFlat

Neither? I suggested exposing the gradient resource, from which you can implicitly create a texture inside of the stylebox implementation.

We should leverage it, not muddy its strengths. And if the two styleboxes need to be merged into one, then that's a different discussion. Right, but if we implemented these PR's explicitly for each use-case like you said, and got to a situation where styleboxflat has gradient support (which I really want!) and styleboxtexture has support for rounded corners and shadows (for which I can think of a lot of use-cases!), we'd have a situation where there's 2 styleboxes with 80% overlap in features, differing only in that styleboxflat doesn't have texture-support, and styleboxtexture doesn't have borders. 

It's not obvious to me that the above situation would be less "muddy" than just giving one stylebox 100% of features. Especially since the separation between parametrically creating a flat design vs hand-drawing would imo already be broken once we added rounded corners/shadows to styleboxtexture.

Anyway, I agree completely with you that having a build in solution for easily layering styleboxes would be ideal! If that existed this discussion would largely be moot I think.

> we'd have a situation where there's 2 styleboxes with 80% overlap in features, differing only in that styleboxflat doesn't have texture-support, and styleboxtexture doesn't have borders.

Exactly this. I don't think it's possible to replicate the functionality in this PR without creating a stylebox that has a ton of feature overlap.

Personally, I'd love to see this merged, as from the examples shown, it looks incredibly powerful and would be a perfect fit for some of the things I'm trying to do in my games.
I really like this how it is. Ive never liked that there was a separate texture stylebox, just felt like unnecessary friction to create the looks that I want to create.

Interesting debate with that feature overlap.

- StyleBoxFlat has the rounded corners, separate border, drop shadow, but solid colors only (before this PR)
- StyleBoxTexture supports 9-patch slicing, but no corners, no borders, no shadow.

I think we should come to expanding the possibilities rather than splitting the use cases by principle, while keeping an eye on having the resources naming relevant.

StyleBoxTexture still has its edge for 9-patch slicing - something many forgot about in the era of flat design, but definitely relevant to create extensible boxes with a stretched center and fixed border sizes out of a single graphic.

Now, with this PR, StyleBoxFlat opens possibilities to spin up design ideas quickly, and this is definitely a plus. Examples:

- Texture and border, with independent rendering of the borders i.e. no need to have those present in the texture. Makes it easy to pick any "flat" texture not initially made for a bordered block.
- Texture and rounded corners, without the need to have the corners cut off inside the texture
- Clean rendering of the rounded corners with a texture, for example if the image is upscaled
- Texture + border + rounded corners all on the same rendering, without the bleeding at the corners that would happen if two separate renderings of the texture and the border would happen layered on top of each other after the corner crop is applied on each one (caused by alpha pixels on the edges)

The easy gradients also open up new possibilities for creating editor themes with those without having to ship image textures along. At least, I hope so!

FYI, three years ago, I sketched an implementation of extensions for StyleBoxFlat that may be complementary to the additions of this PR. https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6812. It has remained stale so far. Feel free to get inspiration. It includes:

- Separate border coloring per side, to make a "line on one side" or imitate button bevels in older operating systems
- A StyleBoxStack that renders multiple stacked StyleBoxes in one place, to make a composite drawing. But it led to other hurdles I was not able to overcome at the moment, such as making a proper UI to edit the stack and apply margins to each layer. Useful to make a double border, or a border on top of a texture.

> Personally, I'd love to see this merged, as from the examples shown, it looks incredibly powerful and would be a perfect fit for some of the things I'm trying to do in my games.

Please note that with my suggestions implemented none of the examples shown would be affected.

-----

> I think we should come to expanding the possibilities rather than splitting the use cases by principle

Expanding of possibilities does not necessarily come from adding dozens new features to a single class. Adding requested features to appropriate classes still expands what you can achieve with built-in styleboxes, and indeed a separate `StyleBox` type that supports layering/stacking, as we both agree, would be a more powerful way to combine multiple effects together, in a controlled manner, without putting every possible permutation in `StyleBoxFlat`.

> StyleBoxTexture still has its edge for 9-patch slicing

Something also has to be said about having full texture support without 9-patch support then. Styleboxes are used on resizable panels and without 9-patch support, I'm not sure there are meaningful design applications to other types of textures, other than gradients. So then that remaining edge that `StyleBoxTexture` has should also be incorporated here, and then what's left?

I maintain the position that we should add gradient support, not gradient/full texture support to flats; implement rounded corners support to texture; implement a `StyleBox` subtype that allows layering of any number of other styleboxes. And it seems to me that the main argument against this suggestion is the fear that this would be meaningfully limiting in some way, which I do not agree with personally. I believe, if implemented, users would be fully satisfied with such solution.

> without 9-patch support, I'm not sure there are meaningful design applications to other types of textures, other than gradients. You can quickly pick a texture representing some kind of material out of a library, which does not have a border, and associate it with a border drawn by the StyleBox itself without having to use a graphics software to bake the border into one single image. The stretch mode of the background texture can be kept independent. The texture is also able to stretch or tile within the corner territory of an equivalent 9-patch. When using the layered approach with rounded corners, there can be an unwanted color bleed, due to the way semitransparent pixels stack each other. I simulated the glitch using a graphics editor. What I did is draw a rounded rectangle that contains what would be the texture (the red stripes), then draw the blue frame on a different layer on top with the exact same corner radius. You can notice, that, on the top left, there is a bleed of the red pixels with the checkered background. First image has the glitch that would be the result of layering. Second image ideal solution that the current proposal of the PR is able to achieve out-of-the-box AFAIK.

> Expanding of possibilities does not necessarily come from adding dozens new features to a single class. Adding requested features to appropriate classes still expands what you can achieve with built-in styleboxes, and indeed a separate `StyleBox` type that supports layering/stacking, as we both agree, would be a more powerful way to combine multiple effects together, in a controlled manner, without putting every possible permutation in `StyleBoxFlat`.

I don't think this is a very fair characterization of the arguments for adding texture support to StyleboxFlat. 
But I care much more about adding Gradient support, so if Texture-support is a blocker for people I'm fine with it being left out of this pr.

@davthedev I'm not sure why you think there would be a visual difference when it's two separate styleboxes drawn on top of each other. The background and the border are drawn separately as is. And styleboxes are not even the owner of the drawing context, the `CanvasItem` that draws them is. You can just as well call the same draw commands within the canvas item's `NOTIFICATION_DRAW`. It's just that the stylebox is a neat abstraction of these calls.

Anyway, the part that you have quoted doesn't argue against use cases where you want to add a border to a borderless texture. It argues that there is not much use in having a background texture on a resizable panel that you cannot 9-patch slice. You can't even control whether it should be tiled or stretched right now.

One argument for adding texture support to StyleBoxFlat is to draw images with rounded corners. This would be helpful for asset store thumbnails in the editor: Right now, the placeholder has rounded corners but the actual thumbnail doesn't. There are workarounds for this, but they all have downsides of their own: - Custom shader: Requires a fair amount of extra code, especially with antialiased corners. - CanvasItem Clip Children + StyleBoxFlat used as alpha mask: Slow for dozens of thumbnails, since it requires a lot of framebuffer copies. - Manipulating image on the CPU at load-time: Slow, not vector-based.
Really hope this can be re-evaluated and merged! The PR is a must have if you want a gradient with rounded corners
Agreed. Found one workaround for it but it's not a pretty one and would've been far easier with this PR.

When blending, the border blends only to the Color not the combined final Color/Texture. Would it be possible to blend to the final result? As this would open up some nice skeuomorphic possibilities. e.g. desired result, which currently has to be created with 9 patch rects, and therefore doesn't scale to different resolutions as easily as if it was defined by gradients directly.
@GeordieTomo Couldn't you already make the desired result with this pr? I can't really tell what part of that window requires the border to blend to a BG texture.

@GeordieTomo I'm not sure the best way to get what you're describing. Currently border_blend just transitions from border_color to bg_color, and with this PR, if there's a texture on border_texture and/or bg_texture, they just get modulated.  

We'd probably need a custom border_blend behavior, which is a different feature. 

Also keep in mind, Gradient textures are still textures, so they may have the same scaling issues you mentioned

I think this PR had those features implemented. Maybe some of them can be salvaged https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/77215

Just decided to test this PR after remembering it, it solves the one issue that had turned me off from working on a project. I was designing a TV UI inspired by TiVo's set top box UI, and one of the things I wanted to try to do was to create a godot-only solution of stylizing the UI. I was only using StyleBoxFlats for these, and I ran into a brick wall when trying to create stacked gradients... it just wasn't viable. Trying to use a GradientTexture2D wasn't exactly viable either, I just couldn't get it to look right. With this PR, I was able to create an entirely native solution for this. Sure, I could've created a separate 9rect texture and just used that, but I see this PR the same way I see LabelSettings' stacked effects: It's just a native way of creating layered effects that's faster and allows for better rapid iteration than the alternatives. I also tried merging this into the current master, but it created an error every time I tried to compile it. Reference (Copyrighted material redacted) 4.7, StyleboxFlat 4.7, This PR, plus rounded corners.
